Sampled ranking metrics measure performance against the sampled candidates; they need not preserve full-catalog model rankings, even in expectation ([Krichene & Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). For paired perturbation diagnostics, keep each user’s target and candidate set identical before/after perturbation. Adapting [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/), resample users with replacement while retaining their paired outcomes; cluster multiple observations from the same user. For this four-category benchmark, resample users within each category and recompute the equal-weight macro-average difference. Interpretation: uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and realized candidate sets; excludes retraining variability and negative-sampling variability. Bootstrap replicates neither retrain nor combine predictors.

Sequence shuffling has been used to probe sequential structure ([Does It Look Sequential?](https://publications.hse.ru/en/chapters/984043670)). For a fixed model, however, inference-time perturbation measures sensitivity to changed inputs, potentially outside its training distribution; a performance drop alone does not establish causal dependence on sequence order. Distinguish target-item exposure elsewhere in training, legitimate repeated consumption, and exposure to the exact evaluated user–target interaction. The last makes the probe partly an in-sample recall/memorization diagnostic, rather than evidence of unseen-interaction generalization; item exposure alone does not establish leakage. Report exposure status, paired effect sizes and confidence intervals, and perturbation details. Preserve item multiplicities, sequence length, padding and targets when isolating order effects; separate order changes from deletions or recency changes. These are methodological implications for the proposed diagnostic, not findings about the current models.
